I will keep it simple and steady this year. In Quzhou, the land, water, and weather fit the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation best, and at my age I would rather grow crops I know well, that are easier to manage, easier to sell, and less risky than trying something fancy. So I will keep winter wheat on the land first, then follow it with summer maize after harvest. I will use improved or hybrid seed because it gives me more stable emergence and yield, but I will not push inputs too hard because fertilizer, water, and pesticide all cost money. I will plough before wheat to turn the soil and hold moisture better, then use rotary tillage before maize because it is faster after wheat harvest. I will fertilize mainly as base fertilizer and then topdress nitrogen at key stages, irrigate only when the crop really needs it, and spray only when pests or disease pressure is clear. My goal is not maximum yield on paper. My goal is a crop I can finish safely, sell easily, and harvest with fewer surprises.
